title: Reading the Word
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Reading the Word is the regular receiving of Scripture as God’s written truth for faith, worship, obedience, correction, and hope. God’s people are called to hear and read His Word so their lives are shaped by Him.
summary: Reading the Word is the regular receiving of Scripture as God’s written truth for faith, worship, obedience, correction, and hope. God’s people are called to hear and read His Word so their lives are shaped by Him.
christFocus: The written Word leads readers to the living Christ. As believers read Scripture, they learn who Jesus is, what He has done, what He commands, and how to follow Him faithfully.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s people are called to be people of the Word. Scripture is not meant to remain closed, forgotten, or reserved only for leaders. It is to be read, heard, treasured, taught, and obeyed.

Regular reading forms the heart over time. God’s Word exposes sin, renews thinking, strengthens faith, reveals God’s character, and teaches believers how to walk before Him. Reading Scripture is not a religious box to check; it is a means of life with God.

Throughout Scripture, God’s people are instructed to read and hear His Word. Kings, leaders, families, churches, and ordinary believers all need the steady influence of God’s truth.

Reading the Word also prepares believers for obedience. Scripture is not given merely to increase knowledge, but to shape the life of faith. The blessed reader is the one who hears and keeps what God has spoken.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers are spiritually weak not because God has been silent, but because His Word is neglected. Without regular exposure to Scripture, people become more easily shaped by fear, culture, temptation, entertainment, and false teaching.

This doctrine encourages simple faithfulness. A believer does not need to master everything at once. Opening the Word consistently, humbly, and prayerfully is one of the ordinary ways God strengthens His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Make Scripture reading a regular part of your life with God. Begin where you are, not where you wish you were. Read with attention, prayer, humility, and a desire to obey. Let the Word of God slowly reshape your thinking, priorities, desires, and trust in Christ.
